text:
maria: FYI customer ac-8472 reporting a sudden spike in decrypt failures after a scheduled KMS rotation. Happening on their Private deployment in eu-west-1.

sam: Can you paste CloudTrail/app logs? Any error codes (AccessDenied vs InvalidCiphertext)? :thinking:

maria: CloudTrail shows KMS Decrypt -> InvalidCiphertextException. Caller = arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/redwood-private-proxy/xyz. App logs: "decrypt failed: invalid ciphertext". They include an encryptionContext {"tenant":"ac-8472","bucket":"prod"}.

dave: Did they perform alias swap (alias -> new-key) or rewrap objects? Important to know how rotation was done.

jen: Customer says they created a new CMK and updated the alias to point at it via Console. They did not re-encrypt persisted blobs.

sam: That is likely root cause. If blobs were encrypted with the old key material, swapping alias without re-encrypt means alias points to a different CMK and decrypts will fail.

maria: Repro steps I ran against a sample blob:
1) Pulled ciphertext from S3 to file blob.bin
2) aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --encryption-context '{"tenant":"ac-8472","bucket":"prod"}' --key-id alias/redwood-ac-8472
Result: InvalidCiphertextException

Then: aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --encryption-context '{"tenant":"ac-8472","bucket":"prod"}' --key-id <old-key-id>
Result: SUCCESS and plaintext returned.

jen: That confirms alias now points to new key; old key still holds material for existing ciphertext. Did they disable or schedule deletion for old key?

dave: Check key state and rotation status:

Commands: 
```
aws kms describe-key --key-id <old-key-id>
aws kms list-aliases --key-id alias/redwood-ac-8472
aws kms list-grants --key-id <old-key-id>
aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <old-key-id>
```

maria: I checked — old-key-id is DISABLED and a deletion window was scheduled (7 days). That matches their timeline.

sam: Short-term mitigation: re-enable old key + cancel deletion if within window, so reads succeed again via explicit key-id or until we re-encrypt.

dave: Ops commands to recover quickly: 
```
aws kms enable-key --key-id <old-key-id>
aws kms cancel-key-deletion --key-id <old-key-id>
```

jen: Also audit CloudTrail for CreateAlias/UpdateAlias/DeleteAlias timestamps so we can correlate. We should surface this to the customer as the action that caused the outage.

maria: Customer code uses header x-redwood-kms-enc which is base64 JSON. They sent: eyJ0ZW5hbnQiOiJhYy04NDcyIiwiYnVja2V0IjoicHJvZCJ9 -> decodes to {"tenant":"ac-8472","bucket":"prod"}, so encryptionContext matches. Not a CB mismatch.

sam: Note: encryptionContext mismatch would give AccessDenied/InvalidCiphertext depending on KMS; but here we validated it matches. The blob only decrypts with old key material.

dave: Action items: 
- dave: try re-enable old key + verify decrypt with sample blob (30m)
- sam: collect CloudTrail alias swap events and list of affected S3 prefixes (15m)
- maria: coord customer comms and recommend canceling deletion + re-encrypt backlog (15m)
- jen: draft alias-swap runbook to avoid future outages (60m)
- eng-oncall: prepare rollback plan for alias mapping if re-enable fails

kms-bot: Incident created INC-2026-1091 (P1) — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-1091 :rotating_light:

maria: I re-enabled the old key and tested decrypt — success on sample. Pushed instructions to customer to run re-encrypt for existing objects. :white_check_mark:

jen: Suggested re-encrypt snippet for customer (re-encrypt keeps contexts):
```
aws kms re-encrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin \
  --source-key-id <old-key-id> \
  --destination-key-id <new-key-id> \
  --source-encryption-context '{"tenant":"ac-8472","bucket":"prod"}' \
  --destination-encryption-context '{"tenant":"ac-8472","bucket":"prod"}'
```

sam: Long-term: add an alert for alias changes on CMKs used by Private customers and add a pre-deploy checklist preventing alias swap until re-encryption is completed. cc @infra.

dave: Also check for grants that might have been revoked during the swap; if customers used grants instead of key policy we need to ensure grant tokens were preserved.

maria: Customer will cancel deletion and run re-encrypt over night. I'll update ticket after they confirm. Thanks team. :pray:
